title: Categorical characterization of the Schroeder-Bernstein property

problemStatement.formal: Let C be a locally small category. C has the Schroeder-Bernstein property (SBP) iff for all X, Y in Ob(C), the existence of monos m : X → Y and n : Y → X implies X ≅ Y. Identify a minimal categorical hypothesis Φ(C) such that Φ(C) ⇒ SBP. Banaschewski–Brümmer (1986) gave one sufficient condition (the split-mono / retraction condition).
problemStatement.plain: Schroeder-Bernstein in Set says: mutual injections imply a bijection. In many concrete categories (groups, Banach spaces) this fails. The open question is: what is the right categorical hypothesis that recovers the property? Banaschewski and Brümmer (1986) showed a 'split-mono' axiom suffices; a complete (necessary + sufficient) characterization is open.
whyMatters: Foundational categorical question with concrete failure witnesses (Bumby, Gowers).
Direct extension of a fully verified Wiedijk-100 gallery entry (Schroeder–Bernstein in Set).
Mathlib currently has zero infrastructure for SBP in arbitrary categories — the gap is wide open.

proven: Categories with the split-mono / retraction condition have SBP (Banaschewski–Brümmer 1986).
open: Necessary + sufficient categorical conditions for SBP (i.e. a complete characterization).
Whether the split-mono condition is strictly weaker than 'topos'.

insights: SBP fails in concrete categories with structure (Grp, Ban) but holds in pure Set; the categorical 'right hypothesis' isolates the structure-free skeleton.
The split-mono / retraction condition (Banaschewski–Brümmer 1986) is the cleanest known sufficient condition: every mono splits ⇒ SBP, via a short composition argument.
Mathlib's CategoryTheory.SplitMono cleanly models the hypothesis; the Lean formalization should be ~80 LOC.

In Type u (v4.26.0), CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective lives in Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Types.Basic and reduces categorical SBP to Function.Embedding.antisymm in three lines — no glue needed beyond the Equiv.toIso lift.

Honesty caveat for S4: the literal statement '[every mono splits] → HasSBP C' collapses Mono = Iso (via the equation m ∘ r ∘ m = m and mono-cancellation), making the conclusion vacuous. The S4 PR should either use regular-mono variants or document the collapse.

TopCat is the first Lean-formal HasSBP failure witness: [0,1] and (0,1) admit mutual continuous injections (compression (x+1)/4 and inclusion) but compactness blocks homeomorphism. The proof chains TopCat.mono_iff_injective → HasSBP destructor → TopCat.homeoOfIso → Homeomorph.compactSpace → isCompact_Ioo_iff (~13 LOC body).

The TopCat counterexample uses topological structure where the underlying set bijection ([0,1] ≅_Set (0,1) via the same Schroeder-Bernstein machinery hasSBP_Type proves) is incompatible with the topology — making it a direct analogue of Bumby (Grp) and Gowers (Ban) but realised in a category Mathlib formalises explicitly.
mathlibGaps: No HasSchroederBernsteinProperty class in Mathlib upstream (filled locally by SchroederBernsteinOQ01.HasSBP).
No Mathlib-upstream theorem connecting CategoryTheory.mono_iff_injective directly to Function.Embedding.antisymm; the bridge had to be written by hand.
No formal failure witness in any concrete category (Bumby's Grp counterexample, Gowers' Ban counterexample) — remain at the literature-citation level.
